extracted.intended_audience: literate general public interested in travel, international affairs, and the mid-19th-century peace movement
extracted.subtask_description: A mid-19th-century travel narrative that includes reportage and commentary on the Universal Peace Congress and contemporary public policy; combines observational travel writing with prescriptive resolutions and political argumentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of religious instructors and the press to diffuse pacific principles
rubrics_metrics.description: That it is the special and solemn duty of all Ministers of Religion, Instructors of Youth, and Conductors of the Public Press, to employ their great influence in the diffusion of pacific principles and sentiments, and in eradicating from the minds of men those hereditary animosities, and political and commercial jealousies, which have been so often the cause of disastrous Wars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as Resolution 1 of the Congress; frames moral actors (clergy, teachers, press) as responsible agents for fostering peace by shaping opinion and removing causes of international animosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer interstate disputes to competent and impartial arbitrators
rubrics_metrics.description: That as an appeal to the sword can settle no question, on any principle of equity and right, it is the duty of Governments to refer to the decision of competent and impartial Arbitrators such differences arising between them as cannot be otherwise amicably adjusted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolution 2; prescribes arbitration as the proper mechanism for interstate dispute settlement in place of armed conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: International disarmament / reduction of standing armaments
rubrics_metrics.description: That the Standing Armaments, with which the Governments of Europe menace each other, amid professions of mutual friendship and confidence, being a prolific source of social immorality, financial embarrassment, and national suffering, while they excite constant disquietude and irritation among the nations, this Congress would earnestly urge upon the Governments the imperative necessity of entering upon a system of International Disarmament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolution 3; links standing armies to moral and fiscal harms and urges governments to pursue systematic disarmament as a policy to reduce tensions and suffering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condemnation of war loans and loans for armaments
rubrics_metrics.description: This Congress, regarding the system of negotiating Loans for the prosecution of War, or the maintenance of warlike armaments, as immoral in principle and disastrous in operation, renews its emphatic condemnation of all such Loans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolution 4; treats financial instruments that fund war or standing armaments as morally and practically objectionable and calls for their public repudiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute non-intervention in other states' domestic affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: This Congress, believing that the intervention, by threatened or actual violence, of one country in the international politics of another, is a frequent cause of bitter and desolating wars, maintains that the right of every State to regulate its own affairs should be held absolute and inviolate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolution 5; affirms a principle of state sovereignty and condemns violent intervention as a major cause of war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare public opinion for an authoritative Code of International Law
rubrics_metrics.description: This Congress recommends all the friends of Peace to prepare public opinion, in their respective countries, with a view to the formation of an authoritative Code of International Law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolution 6; promotes normative and institutional development (an international legal code) and calls on peace advocates to cultivate domestic public support for it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condemn aggression upon aboriginal and feeble tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: This Congress expresses its strong abhorrence of the system of aggression and violence practiced by so-called civilized nations upon aboriginal and feeble tribes, as leading to incessant and exterminating wars, eminently unfavorable to the true progress of religion, civilization and commerce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolution 7; singles out colonial/imperial aggression as morally abhorrent and practically counterproductive to civilization and commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote international exhibitions and intercourse to foster peace
rubrics_metrics.description: This Congress, convinced that whatever brings the nations of the earth together in intimate and friendly intercourse must tend to the establishment of Peace, by removing misapprehensions and prejudices, and inspiring mutual respect, hails, with unqualified satisfaction, the Exhibition of the Industry of all Nations, as eminently calculated to promote that end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolution 8; endorses cultural and commercial exchange (e.g., world's exhibitions) as tools for reducing misunderstanding and building peaceful relations between nations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use peace societies to return peace-friendly parliamentary representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: That the members of Peace Societies, in all Constitutional Countries, be recommended to use their influence to return to their respective Parliaments, representatives who are friends of Peace, and who will be prepared to support, by their votes, measures for the diminution of the number of men employed in, and the amount of money expended for, War purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolution 9; a practical civic-political strategy: electoral action to change parliamentary composition and reduce military expenditure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirm right to resist invasion or intolerable oppression (proposed)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Resolved, That in commending to all men everywhere the duty of seeking and preserving Peace, we bear in mind the Apostle's injunction, 'First pure, then peaceable,' and do not deny but affirm the right of a Nation wantonly invaded by a foreign army, or intolerably oppressed by its own rulers, to resist force by force."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An author-proposed resolution appended to the report: qualifies pacifist advocacy by recognizing a right of self-defense and resistance to tyrannical rulers; frames a threshold for when force may be justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbandment/dispersion of standing armies urged by speakers
rubrics_metrics.description: Speakers (e.g., Mr. Cobden, others) urged that the demoralizing influence of Armies and the expensiveness and immorality of Standing Armies argue for their entire disbandment and dispersion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported advocacy from Congress speeches: standing armies are framed as morally corrupting and fiscally ruinous; disbandment is put forward as a desirable policy outcome consistent with pacific principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: National policy preference: invest in education and social improvement over fortifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Any nation, by wisely expending half so much in systematic efforts to educate, employ steadily and reward amply its poorer classes, would have been strengthened and ensured against invasion far more than it could be by walls like precipices and a belt of fortresses as impregnable as Gibraltar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author's broader prescriptive claim about national security and public policy: social investment (education, employment, fair reward) is superior protection to heavy military fortifications; presented as practical wisdom for rulers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customs-house scrutiny should be expeditious and rational
rubrics_metrics.description: Our baggage underwent a new custom-house scrutiny, which was expeditiously and rationally made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An implicitly stated standard for border/customs procedures: inspections ought to be prompt and reasonable to facilitate travel and commerce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and adequacy of passenger steamers (implicit public-standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaint that the Channel boats were 'little black, cobbling concerns' with no berths and inadequate accommodation for passengers; an appeal that better steamboat-building is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit consumer/public-service criterion: vessels on important international routes should be properly built, sized, and furnished to provide safe and decent accommodations for passengers; poor quality is viewed as anachronistic and unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social virtue: simplicity, frankness, and absence of pretence in manners
rubrics_metrics.description: The absence of pretense, of stateliness, of a desire to be thought a personage ... The Germans ... render to rank or dignity no more homage than is necessary—their souls are still free, and their manners evince a simplicity and frankness which might shame or at least instruct America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorial normative standard for personal and civic manners: humility, simplicity, and frankness are praised as socially and morally superior to aristocratic pretension.
